title: How to Seal Drafty Windows

seo.title: How to Seal Drafty Windows
seo.meta_description: A drafty window can leak air through moving sashes, frame joints, or gaps around the window unit.
seo.search_intent: Use a practical method for how to seal drafty windows, protecting materials and equipment and knowing when to stop or change approach.

excerpt: A drafty window can leak air through moving sashes, frame joints, or gaps around the window unit. Locating the exact leak lets you choose weatherstripping, caulk, or repair without blocking drainage paths or moving parts.
content_html:
A drafty window can leak air through moving sashes, frame joints, or gaps around the window unit. Locating the exact leak lets you choose weatherstripping, caulk, or repair without blocking drainage paths or moving parts.

Find the leak on a windy day

Move your hand slowly around the sash, frame, and trim or use a lightweight strip of tissue to detect airflow. Do not use an open flame near curtains or finishes to hunt for drafts.

Use weatherstripping on moving joints

Sashes and operable joints need compressible weatherstripping that seals when closed but still allows movement. Choose a thickness that closes the gap without straining hardware or preventing the window from latching.

Caulk fixed gaps with a compatible sealant

Fixed joints between the frame and trim can be caulked when clean and dry. Do not block weep holes, vents, or channels designed to drain water from the window assembly.

A draft may come from behind the trim

If air comes through trim even though visible joints are sealed, insulation may be missing around the window. Removing trim or adding foam requires control of expansion and moisture; installation defects may need broader repair.

faq.question: How can I pinpoint where a window draft is entering?
faq.answer: Move your hand slowly around the sash, frame, and trim or use a lightweight strip of tissue to detect airflow. Do not use an open flame near curtains or finishes to hunt for drafts.

faq.question: When should I use weatherstripping instead of caulk?
faq.answer: Sashes and operable joints need compressible weatherstripping that seals when closed but still allows movement. Choose a thickness that closes the gap without straining hardware or preventing the window from latching.

faq.question: What does it mean if the draft seems to come from behind the trim?
faq.answer: If air comes through trim even though visible joints are sealed, insulation may be missing around the window. Removing trim or adding foam requires control of expansion and moisture; installation defects may need broader repair.
